html:
The first Olympic Games, held by tradition in 776 BCE at Olympia, a sanctuary of Zeus in the western Peloponnese. The date comes from lists of winners drawn up centuries later, and is uncertain. The first recorded champion, Koroibos of Elis, won the only event, a foot race of one stade, about 190 m.

The games were held every four years, and Greeks later counted years in Olympiads from 776 BCE. A sacred truce let athletes and visitors travel safely. Over time the program grew to include wrestling, boxing, the pentathlon and chariot races. Only free Greek men could compete, and they competed naked.

The festival bound the scattered Greek city-states together in shared religion and rivalry, as the oracle at Delphi did. The great Temple of Zeus was built there in the 400s BCE. The games ran for over a thousand years, until Christian emperors such as Theodosius I ended pagan festivals, around 393 CE or a little later. They were revived as the modern Olympics at Athens in 1896.
